info.description: Program five moves in advance and send your robot racing across a factory floor full of conveyor belts, gears, pits and lasers. Everybody reveals their programmed moves at the same time, so robots shove each other into the machinery all the time. First robot to touch the three checkpoints in order wins.
info.ruleText:
Two to six robots race across a factory floor to three checkpoints. Every round each player is dealt nine program cards, secretly programs five of them into five registers and then all registers are revealed and executed one after the other, in the priority order printed on the cards.

After every register the factory acts: conveyor belts carry robots along, gears rotate them, walls stop them and lasers damage them. Damage removes cards from your next hand and finally locks registers, so a battered robot becomes harder to steer. Robots push each other, and a robot that is pushed into a pit or over the edge is destroyed, loses a life and returns on its last checkpoint. The first robot to touch checkpoint 3 wins.
info.helpText:
Goal

Steer your robot across the factory floor and touch the three numbered checkpoints in order (1, then 2, then 3). The first robot to reach checkpoint 3 wins. Nobody actually steers directly: you program five moves in advance and then watch what happens.

Getting started

Everybody takes a seat first (the six seats are on the right, the robot with the matching number and color appears on its docking bay at the bottom of the board). Then any player presses the restart button – that places all robots, shuffles the deck and deals the first hands.

A round

  1. Every player is dealt nine program cards into the hand at the bottom of the table (one card less for each damage). Only you can see your own hand.
  2. Drag five cards from your hand into your five register slots on the right. They are placed face down – only you can see what you programmed. Your seat glows until all five registers are filled.
  3. Press the big ▶ button once per register. The register is revealed for everybody and executed in priority order (the number printed on the card, highest first), then the board elements act: express belts move two spaces, normal belts one, gears turn robots, lasers fire and checkpoints are registered.
  4. After the fifth register the round ends automatically: robots on a wrench or a checkpoint repair one damage, all cards are shuffled back, destroyed robots return and new hands are dealt.

Buttons

  • ▶ reveal and execute the next register (this is the only button you need during a round).
  • Cards end the current round by hand: discard, repair, respawn and deal new hands.
  • Power announces a power down for the next round: you get no cards, but all your damage is repaired. Press it again to cancel. A yellow power icon next to your status shows that it is armed.
  • Restart starts a completely new game.

Status displays

Next to every seat: wrench = damage, robot = lives left, flag = checkpoints touched. From five damage on, registers lock from the right; a locked register turns red and keeps its card for the next round. At ten damage the robot is destroyed, it loses a life and comes back on its archive marker with two damage (the archive marker is the last checkpoint or wrench the robot stood on, or its docking bay). A destroyed robot waits next to its registers until the next round; a player who has lost all three lives is out of the game.

Doing it yourself

Nothing is forced. Every robot can simply be dragged to another cell at any time and clicking your own robot turns it 90° clockwise, so you can correct the automation or play completely by hand. The next time a register is executed the automation picks up the positions you set.

Board

Gray arrows are conveyor belts (one space), blue arrows with a 2 are express belts (two spaces), curved arrows on a belt turn the robot. Amber circles are gears that turn robots, black cells are pits, green wrenches repair one damage at the end of a round, yellow bars are walls that block movement and lasers, and red laser emitters shoot along their row or column. Falling into a pit or off the edge destroys a robot.

fields.text: All robots return to their docking bays and all cards are shuffled back into the deck.

stepRoutine: // moves robot <sid> one cell towards <sd>, pushing robots in the way
moveNRoutine: // moves robot <mr> <mn> cells into its facing direction
destroyRoutine: // removes robot <dr> from the board until the next round
checkDeathsRoutine: // destroys every robot that stands on a pit or fell off the board
rayRoutine: // follows a laser beam from <rx>,<ry> towards <rd>; result is the robot it hits
laserRoutine: // fires all robot lasers and all board lasers
beltRoutine: // moves robots on conveyors; <bm> is X for express belts only, A for all belts
gearRoutine: // rotates robots that stand on a gear
readyRoutine: // makes the seat of player <rn> glow while the registers are not full
dealRoutine: // deals 9 cards minus damage to every player
newRoundRoutine: // end of round: repairs, discard, respawn and deal again
respawnRoutine: // puts destroyed robot <sr> back on its archive marker
runRoutine: // reveals and executes the next register
powerRoutine: // announces or cancels a power down for the player pressing the button
